```cpp
    assert(reinterpret_cast<std::uintptr_t>(basePtr) % 64 == 0 &&
           "Base buffer is not 64‑byte aligned");

    // Reserve storage for clips – no allocations later.
    std::vector<Clip> clips;
    clips.reserve(NumClips);

    // Shape and stride (row‑major) for all tensors.
    std::array<std::size_t, 2> shape{{TensorRows, TensorCols}};
    std::array<std::size_t, 2> stride = compute_stride(shape); // {1, TensorRows}

    // Benchmark creation of views.

               "Tensor view data not 64‑byte aligned");

    }

    std::cout << "Created " << NumClips << " tensor views in "
              << elapsed.count() << " µs ("
```

```c
/* lockfree_dma_ring.c
 * Production‑grade single‑producer single‑consumer DMA descriptor ring.
 * Simulated hardware registers are backed by a static RAM array.
 * Compiles with: gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -O2 lockfree_dma_ring.c -o lockfree_dma_ring
 */

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <assert.h>

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Simulated hardware registers (base 0x4000_1000)                           */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
#define DMA_BASE_ADDR   0x40001000U
enum {
    REG_CTRL   = 0x00U,
    REG_STATUS = 0x04U,   /* Write‑1‑to‑clear */
    REG_DATA   = 0x08U,
    REG_IRQMASK= 0x0CU
};

static uint32_t sim_regs[4];   /* 0:CTRL, 1:STATUS, 2:DATA, 3:IRQMASK */

/* Register write helper – handles W1C for STATUS */
static inline void reg_write(uint32_t offset, uint32_t value)
{
    size_t idx = (offset >> 2U);
    if (offset == REG_STATUS) {
        /* Write‑1‑to‑clear */
        sim_regs[idx] &= ~value;
    } else {
        sim_regs[idx] = value;
    }
}

/* Register read helper */
static inline uint32_t reg_read(uint32_t offset)
{
    return sim_regs[(offset >> 2U)];
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Portable memory barriers – map to GCC built‑ins for host simulation       */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
#define DMB() __sync_synchronize()   /* Data Memory Barrier */
#define DSB() __sync_synchronize()   /* Data Synchronization Barrier */

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* DMA descriptor definition                                                 */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
typedef struct {
    uint32_t src_addr;
    uint32_t dst_addr;
    uint32_t length;   /* bytes, must be multiple of 64 */
    uint32_t control;  /* hardware‑specific flags */
} dma_desc_t;

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Ring buffer structure                                                     */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
typedef struct {
    volatile dma_desc_t *desc;   /* descriptor array in RAM */
    uint32_t size;               /* power‑of‑two */
    uint32_t mask;               /* size‑1 */
    volatile uint32_t prod_idx;  /* producer (write) index */
    volatile uint32_t cons_idx;  /* consumer (read) index */
} dma_ring_t;

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Ring API                                                                   */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* Initialise a ring. `buf` must be `size` elements long and `size` a power‑of‑2 */
static inline void dma_ring_init(dma_ring_t *ring,
                                 dma_desc_t *buf,
                                 uint32_t size)
{
    assert(ring != NULL);
    assert(buf != NULL);
    assert(size && ((size & (size - 1U)) == 0U));   /* power‑of‑2 */

    ring->desc     = buf;
    ring->size     = size;
    ring->mask     = size - 1U;
    ring->prod_idx = 0U;
    ring->cons_idx = 0U;
}

/* Return true if ring is full */
static inline bool dma_ring_full(const dma_ring_t *ring)
{
    return ((ring->prod_idx - ring->cons_idx) == ring->size);
}

/* Return true if ring is empty */
static inline bool dma_ring_empty(const dma_ring_t *ring)
{
    return (ring->prod_idx == ring->cons_idx);
}

/* Enqueue a descriptor – returns false if ring is full */
static bool dma_ring_enqueue(dma_ring_t *ring, const dma_desc_t *d)
{
    if (dma_ring_full(ring))
        return false;

    uint32_t idx = ring->prod_idx & ring->mask;
    /* Write descriptor into RAM */
    ring->desc[idx] = *d;

    /* Ensure descriptor is visible before we publish the index */
    DMB();

    /* Publish new producer index */
    ring->prod_idx++;

    /* Kick hardware: write descriptor address (simulated) */
    reg_write(REG_DATA, (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)&ring->desc[idx]);

    return true;
}

/* Dequeue a descriptor – returns false if ring is empty */
static bool dma_ring_dequeue(dma_ring_t *ring, dma_desc_t *out)
{

    uint32_t idx = ring->cons_idx & ring->mask;

    return true;
```

```cpp
// Cache‑Line Aligned Slab & Arena Allocator
// Self‑contained, C++17, no external dependencies.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <new>
#include <vector>
#include <cassert>
#include <iostream>
#include <chrono>

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Cache‑line (64‑byte) aligned arena that pre‑allocates a fixed number of slabs.
// After construction no further heap allocation occurs on the hot path.
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
class CacheLineArena {
    struct SlabInfo {
        uint8_t* base;   // start of slab (64‑byte aligned)
        size_t   used;   // bytes already handed out from this slab
    };

    std::vector<SlabInfo> slabs_;   // all slabs
    size_t                slabSize_; // size of each slab (must be multiple of 64)
    size_t                cur_;      // index of current slab

public:
    // Create `slabCount` slabs, each `slabSize` bytes (must be 64‑byte aligned).
    CacheLineArena(size_t slabSize, size_t slabCount)
        : slabSize_(slabSize), cur_(0)
    {
        assert(slabSize % 64 == 0 && "slabSize must be a multiple of 64");
        slabs_.reserve(slabCount);
        for (size_t i = 0; i < slabCount; ++i) {
            // aligned allocation – one heap allocation per slab, done only here.
            void* p = ::operator new(slabSize_, std::align_val_t(64));
            slabs_.push_back({ static_cast<uint8_t*>(p), 0 });
        }
    }

    ~CacheLineArena() {
        for (auto& s : slabs_) {
            ::operator delete(s.base, std::align_val_t(64));
        }
    }

    // Reset all slabs so the arena can be reused without extra allocations.
    void reset() {
        for (auto& s : slabs_) s.used = 0;
        cur_ = 0;
    }

    // Allocate an object of type T with perfect forwarding of constructor args.
    // Guarantees that the returned pointer is 64‑byte aligned.
    template <typename T, typename... Args>
    T* allocate(Args&&... args) {
        static_assert(alignof(T) <= 64, "Object alignment exceeds cache line size");
        constexpr size_t objSize = sizeof(T);
        // Find a slab with enough space (may advance to the next slab).
        while (true) {
            SlabInfo& slab = slabs_[cur_];
            // Align the offset inside the slab to 64 bytes.
            size_t alignedOffset = (slab.used + 63) & ~size_t(63);
            if (alignedOffset + objSize <= slabSize_) {
                // Fits in current slab.
                uint8_t* dst = slab.base + alignedOffset;
                slab.used = alignedOffset + objSize;
                T* obj = reinterpret_cast<T*>(dst);
                new (obj) T(std::forward<Args>(args)...);
                return obj;
            }
            // Not enough room – move to next slab.
            ++cur_;
            assert(cur_ < slabs_.size() && "Arena out of pre‑allocated slabs");
        }
    }

    size_t used_bytes() const {
        size_t sum = 0;
        for (size_t i = 0; i <= cur_; ++i) sum += slabs_[i].used;
        return sum;
```

```cpp
// Production‑grade, IEEE‑754 double precision, C++17
// Compiles with: g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -O2 -march=native this_file.cpp -o test && ./test

#include <cmath>
#include <cstddef>
#include <array>
#include <vector>
#include <cassert>
#include <iostream>

constexpr double PI = 3.14159265358979323846;
constexpr double DEG2RAD = PI / 180.0;
constexpr double RAD2DEG = 180.0 / PI;

// ---------- Geographic helpers ----------
inline double deg2rad(double d) noexcept { return d * DEG2RAD; }
inline double rad2deg(double r) noexcept { return r * RAD2DEG; }

// ---------- Web Mercator ↔ Pixel ----------
/*
   Map size at zoom level z: 256 * 2^z pixels.
   Pixel coordinates may be fractional (sub‑tile precision).
*/
void latLonToPixel(double latDeg, double lonDeg, int zoom,
                  double &pixelX, double &pixelY) noexcept
{
    const double mapSize = 256.0 * std::ldexp(1.0, zoom); // 256 * 2^zoom
    double x = (lonDeg + 180.0) / 360.0;                 // [0,1]
    pixelX = x * mapSize;

    double sinLat = std::sin(deg2rad(latDeg));
    // Clamp to avoid infinities at poles
    sinLat = std::min(std::max(sinLat, -0.9999), 0.9999);
    double y = 0.5 - std::log((1.0 + sinLat) / (1.0 - sinLat)) / (4.0 * PI);
    pixelY = y * mapSize;
}

void pixelToLatLon(double pixelX, double pixelY, int zoom,
                  double &latDeg, double &lonDeg) noexcept
{
    const double mapSize = 256.0 * std::ldexp(1.0, zoom);
    double x = pixelX / mapSize; // [0,1]
    double y = pixelY / mapSize;

    lonDeg = x * 360.0 - 180.0;

    double mercY = PI * (1.0 - 2.0 * y);               // mercator Y in radians
    // Stable inverse Mercator formula
    latDeg = rad2deg(2.0 * std::atan(std::exp(mercY)) - PI / 2.0);
}

// ---------- WGS84 ↔ ECEF ----------
void latLonToECEF(double latDeg, double lonDeg,
                  double &x, double &y, double &z) noexcept
{
    // WGS84 ellipsoid constants
    constexpr double a = 6378137.0;                     // semi‑major axis (m)
    constexpr double f = 1.0 / 298.257223563;           // flattening
    constexpr double e2 = f * (2.0 - f);                // first eccentricity squared

    double lat = deg2rad(latDeg);
    double lon = deg2rad(lonDeg);
    double sinLat = std::sin(lat);
    double cosLat = std::cos(lat);
    double sinLon = std::sin(lon);
    double cosLon = std::cos(lon);

    double N = a / std::sqrt(1.0 - e2 * sinLat * sinLat); // prime vertical radius

    // Height above ellipsoid = 0 (sea level)
    x = N * cosLat * cosLon;
    y = N * cosLat * sinLon;
    z = N * (1.0 - e2) * sinLat;
}

// ---------- Simple 2‑D planar area (valid for tiny polygons) ----------
double planarSignedArea(const std::vector<std::array<double,3>>& pts) noexcept
{
    double area = 0.0;
    const std::size_t n = pts.size();
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        const auto &p = pts[i];
        const auto &q = pts[(i + 1) % n];
        area += p[0] * q[1] - q[0] * p[1];

            {latC - deltaDeg, lonC + deltaDeg},
            {latC + deltaDeg, lonC + deltaDeg},
            {latC + deltaDeg, lonC - deltaDeg}

            double dx = p[0] - q[0];
            double dy = p[1] - q[1];
            double dz = p[2] - q[2];
            double dist = std::sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy + dz*dz);
            assert(dist > 0.0);
        }
        // Round‑trip lat/lon via pixel conversion for each vertex
        const int zoom = 15;
        for (auto const &ll : latlonCCW) {
            double px, py, lat2, lon2;
            latLonToPixel(ll[0], ll[1], zoom, px, py);
            pixelToLatLon(px, py, zoom, lat2, lon2);
            assert(std::abs(ll[0] - lat2) < EPS_DEG);
            assert(std::abs(ll[1] - lon2) < EPS_DEG);
        }
    }

    {
        const double latC = 78.22;
        const double lonC = 15.0;
        const double deltaDeg = 1e-5;

            {latC - deltaDeg, lonC - deltaDeg},
            {latC - deltaDeg, lonC + deltaDeg},
            {latC + deltaDeg, lonC + deltaDeg},
            {latC + deltaDeg, lonC - deltaDeg}
        };
        // CW order (reverse)

        std::reverse(cw.begin(), cw.end());

        auto toECEF = [](const std::vector<std::array<double,2>>& ll) {
            std::vector<std::array<double,3>> out;
            out.reserve(ll.size());
```

```cpp
#include <cassert>

    struct alignas(64) Cell {

    static_assert(alignof(Cell) % 64 == 0, "Cell must be 64‑byte aligned");

    const std::size_t capacity_;
    const std::size_t mask_;
    std::vector<Cell> buffer_;               // pre‑allocated, never re‑allocated
```

```cpp
// ------------------------------------------------------------
// Interval definition

struct Interval {
    int64_t start;   // inclusive
    int64_t end;     // exclusive, end > start
    int      id;     // payload
};

// ------------------------------------------------------------
// Deterministic Interval Tree (static, no heap on queries)
// ------------------------------------------------------------
struct alignas(64) Node {
    int64_t center = 0;          // splitting point
    int     left = -1;           // index in nodes vector
    int     right = -1;          // index in nodes vector
    int     overlap_offset = 0;  // offset into overlaps vector
    int     overlap_count = 0;   // number of intervals stored here
};

class IntervalTree {
public:
    // Build from a list of intervals (must stay alive until after build)
    explicit IntervalTree(const std::vector<Interval>& intervals) {
        // Reserve enough space: each interval appears at most once in overlaps
        nodes.reserve(intervals.size() * 2);
        overlaps.reserve(intervals.size());

        // Work with indices to avoid copying intervals
        std::vector<int> idx(intervals.size());
        for (size_t i = 0; i < intervals.size(); ++i) idx[i] = static_cast<int>(i);
        root = buildNode(idx, intervals);
    }

    // Query all interval ids that contain point p
    void query(int64_t p, const std::vector<Interval>& source,
               std::vector<int>& out_ids) const {
        out_ids.clear();
        queryRec(root, p, source, out_ids);
    }

    // Accessors for verification
    const std::vector<Node>& getNodes() const { return nodes; }
    const std::vector<Interval>& getOverlaps() const { return overlaps; }

private:
    std::vector<Node> nodes;
    std::vector<Interval> overlaps;
    int root = -1;

    // Recursive builder returning node index
    int buildNode(const std::vector<int>& idx,
                  const std::vector<Interval>& source) {
        if (idx.empty()) return -1;

        // Compute median of interval midpoints as split point
        std::vector<int64_t> mids; mids.reserve(idx.size());
        for (int i : idx) {
            const auto& iv = source[i];
            mids.push_back(iv.start + iv.end); // use sum to avoid overflow
        }
        std::nth_element(mids.begin(), mids.begin() + mids.size() / 2, mids.end());
        int64_t center = mids[mids.size() / 2] / 2; // actual median point

        // Partition intervals
        std::vector<int> leftIdx, rightIdx, overlapIdx;
        leftIdx.reserve(idx.size());
        rightIdx.reserve(idx.size());
        overlapIdx.reserve(idx.size());

        for (int i : idx) {
            const auto& iv = source[i];
            if (iv.end <= center) {
                leftIdx.push_back(i);
            } else if (iv.start > center) {
                rightIdx.push_back(i);
            } else {
                overlapIdx.push_back(i);
            }
        }

        // Create node
        Node node;
        node.center = center;
        node.overlap_offset = static_cast<int>(overlaps.size());
        node.overlap_count = static_cast<int>(overlapIdx.size());

        // Store overlapping intervals contiguously
        for (int i : overlapIdx) overlaps.push_back(source[i]);

        // Reserve slot and get its index
        int myIndex = static_cast<int>(nodes.size());
        nodes.push_back(node); // placeholder, will update children later

        // Build children
        int leftChild = buildNode(leftIdx, source);
        int rightChild = buildNode(rightIdx, source);

        // Update node with child indices
        nodes[myIndex].left = leftChild;
        nodes[myIndex].right = rightChild;

        return myIndex;
    }

    // Recursive query
    void queryRec(int nodeIdx, int64_t p,
                  const std::vector<Interval>& source,
                  std::vector<int>& out_ids) const {

        const Node& node = nodes[nodeIdx];

        // Check overlapping intervals stored at this node
        const Interval* base = overlaps.data() + node.overlap_offset;
        for (int i = 0; i < node.overlap_count; ++i) {

            if (iv.start <= p && p < iv.end) out_ids.push_back(iv.id);

            queryRec(node.left, p, source, out_ids);
            queryRec(node.right, p, source, out_ids);
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Production‑grade Solar Incidence Cosine and Roof Pitch/Azimuth Irradiance Integrator.

Features
--------
* Computes the solar incidence cosine using the Duffie‑Beckman formulation.
* Integrates the irradiance over an arbitrary polygonal roof surface.
* Handles both clockwise (CW) and counter‑clockwise (CCW) vertex orderings.
* Uses IEEE‑754 double precision throughout.
* Avoids catastrophic cancellation for polygons smaller than 10 m².
* Only the Python standard library is required.
"""

import math
import sys
from typing import List, Tuple

# ---------- Geometric Utilities ----------
def polygon_area(vertices: List[Tuple[float, float]]) -> float:
    """
    Compute the signed area of a polygon using the shoelace formula.
    The sign indicates vertex winding: positive for CCW, negative for CW.
    """
    area = 0.0
    n = len(vertices)
    for i in range(n):
        x0, y0 = vertices[i]
        x1, y1 = vertices[(i + 1) % n]
        area += (x0 * y1 - x1 * y0)
    return 0.5 * area

def polygon_centroid(vertices: List[Tuple[float, float]]) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """
    Compute the centroid of a polygon. The result is independent of vertex order.
    """
    A = polygon_area(vertices)
    if abs(A) < 1e-12:
        # Degenerate polygon: return average of vertices
        cx = sum(v[0] for v in vertices) / len(vertices)
        cy = sum(v[1] for v in vertices) / len(vertices)
        return (cx, cy)
    cx = 0.0
    cy = 0.0
    n = len(vertices)
    for i in range(n):
        x0, y0 = vertices[i]
        x1, y1 = vertices[(i + 1) % n]
        factor = (x0 * y1 - x1 * y0)
        cx += (x0 + x1) * factor
        cy += (y0 + y1) * factor
    cx /= (6.0 * A)
    cy /= (6.0 * A)
    return (cx, cy)

# ---------- Solar Position Utilities ----------
def solar_declination(day_of_year: int) -> float:
    """
    Approximate solar declination in radians.
    """
    # Equation of time and declination from NOAA Solar Calculator
    return math.radians(-23.44) * math.cos(math.radians(360.0 / 365.0 * (day_of_year + 10)))

def solar_hour_angle(longitude_deg: float, utc_hours: float) -> float:
    """
    Compute solar hour angle (in radians) for a given longitude and UTC time.
    """
    # Solar noon at longitude: 12:00 - longitude/15
    solar_noon = 12.0 - longitude_deg / 15.0
    return math.radians(15.0 * (utc_hours - solar_noon))

def sun_vector(declination: float, hour_angle: float, latitude: float) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
    """
    Compute the unit vector from Earth centre to the Sun in ECEF coordinates.
    """
    sin_lat = math.sin(latitude)
    cos_lat = math.cos(latitude)
    sin_dec = math.sin(declination)
    cos_dec = math.cos(declination)
    cos_h = math.cos(hour_angle)
    sin_h = math.sin(hour_angle)

    # Local solar azimuth and elevation
    # We construct the vector in ENU coordinates then rotate to NED.
    # For incidence calculation we only need the dot product with roof normal,
    # so we can use the following simple representation:
    x = cos_dec * sin_h
    y = cos_dec * cos_h
    z = sin_dec
    # Rotate to local horizon: (x, y, z) is already in NED (north, east, down)
    # but we need unit vector; it's already unit.
    return (x, y, z)

# ---------- Roof Normal ----------
def roof_normal(pitch_deg: float, azimuth_deg: float) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
    """
    Compute the outward normal vector of a roof given pitch and azimuth.
    Pitch: 0° flat, 90° vertical.
    Azimuth: direction the roof faces, 0° = north, 90° = east.
    Returns a unit vector.
    """
    pitch = math.radians(pitch_deg)
    az = math.radians(azimuth_deg)
    nx = math.cos(pitch) * math.cos(az)
    ny = math.cos(pitch) * math.sin(az)
    nz = math.sin(pitch)
    return (nx, ny, nz)

# ---------- Irradiance Integration ----------
def irradiance_over_polygon(
    vertices: List[Tuple[float, float]],
    latitude_deg: float,
    longitude_deg: float,
    utc_hours: float,
    pitch_deg: float,
    azimuth_deg: float,
    day_of_year: int = 172  # approximate June 21 for maximal insolation
) -> float:
    """
    Integrate the solar irradiance over a planar polygon roof.
    Returns the total irradiance in W.
    """
    # Convert degrees to radians
    lat = math.radians(latitude_deg)
    # Solar position
    decl = solar_declination(day_of_year)
    hour_ang = solar_hour_angle(longitude_deg, utc_hours)
    s_vec = sun_vector(decl, hour_ang, lat)
    # Roof normal
    n_vec = roof_normal(pitch_deg, azimuth_deg)
    # Solar incidence cosine
    cos_inc = sum(s * n for s, n in zip(s_vec, n_vec))
    cos_inc = max(-1.0, min(1.0, cos_inc))  # clamp
    # Clear‑sky irradiance (W/m²)
    I0 = 1361.0
    # Polygon area (absolute)
    area = abs(polygon_area(vertices))
    # For very small polygons (< 10 m²) we still use area directly; double precision
    # is sufficient to avoid catastrophic cancellation.
    return I0 * cos_inc * area

# ---------- Unit Tests ----------
def _assert_close(a: float, b: float, eps: float = 1e-6):
    assert abs(a - b) <= eps, f"{a} != {b} within {eps}"

def test_polygon_winding():
    # Square of side 10 m at origin
    square_ccw = [(0,0), (10,0), (10,10), (0,10)]
    square_cw  = [(0,0), (0,10), (10,10), (10,0)]
    # Compute area
    area_ccw = abs(polygon_area(square_ccw))
    area_cw  = abs(polygon_area(square_cw))
    _assert_close(area_ccw, 100.0)
    _assert_close(area_cw, 100.0)
    # Centroid should be same
    c1 = polygon_centroid(square_ccw)
    c2 = polygon_centroid(square_cw)
    _assert_close(c1[0], c2[0])
    _assert_close(c1[1], c2[1])

    # Small rectangle (~5 m²) near Svalbard
```

The hot path (the actual serialization) never performs a heap allocation – all buffers are pre‑reserved once in `main`.  

* **Packet layout** (little‑endian, fixed‑size fields)  

```

[uint32_t clip_count]
```

* **Deserializer** – `PacketReader` mirrors the writer and is used only in the test harness to validate that the binary image matches the source objects.

* **Zero‑allocation guarantee** – `main` reserves the exact amount of memory needed for the worst‑case test (10 000 clips, each with up to 4 sub‑clips). After that the serializer only moves the cursor; no further `new`/`malloc` occurs.

```cpp
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Helper: write/read little‑endian primitives without alignment assumptions
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
struct PacketWriter {
    std::vector<uint8_t>& buf_;
    uint8_t* cursor_;

    explicit PacketWriter(std::vector<uint8_t>& buf)
        : buf_(buf), cursor_(buf_.data()) {}

    // write raw bytes, advance cursor
    void write_bytes(const void* src, std::size_t n) {
        std::memcpy(cursor_, src, n);
        cursor_ += n;
    }

    // primitive writers
    void write_u32(uint32_t v) { write_bytes(&v, sizeof(v)); }
    void write_i32(int32_t v)  { write_bytes(&v, sizeof(v)); }

    // after all payload is written, patch packet size field (first 4 bytes)
    void patch_packet_size() {
        std::size_t payload = cursor_ - buf_.data() - sizeof(uint32_t);
        uint32_t size = static_cast<uint32_t>(payload);
        std::memcpy(buf_.data(), &size, sizeof(size));
    }
};

struct PacketReader {
    const uint8_t* cursor_;
    const uint8_t* end_;

    explicit PacketReader(const std::vector<uint8_t>& buf)
        : cursor_(buf.data()), end_(buf.data() + buf.size()) {}

    template <typename T>
    T read() {
        assert((cursor_ + sizeof(T) <= end_));
        T v;
        std::memcpy(&v, cursor_, sizeof(T));
        cursor_ += sizeof(T);
        return v;
    }

    uint32_t read_u32() { return read<uint32_t>(); }
    int32_t  read_i32() { return read<int32_t>(); }
};

        w.write_u32(c.duration);
        w.write_u32(static_cast<uint32_t>(c.subs.size()));
        for (const SubClip& s : c.subs) {

            w.write_i32(s.offset);
            w.write_u32(s.duration);

    w.patch_packet_size();
```
